prerequisites: Knowledge from Engineering Mathematics and Physics lectures

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to name and apply fundamental physical laws and methods, as well as basic concepts of fluid mechanics (pressure, density, stationarity, compressibility, viscosity, friction, Mach number, Reynolds number...) for describing properties, flow states, and state changes of simple flows.

Students are able to analyze process engineering flow processes for dominant fluid mechanical effects, classify them, evaluate them regarding available solution possibilities, and critically check the plausibility of the results.
Students are able to apply relevant equations of motion (Bernoulli and continuity equations, impulse theorem) to simple flow problems and make reasonable assumptions.
Students are able to determine acting forces in stationary and moving liquids and gases, and solve problems with moving viscous fluids using force equilibrium on a volume element.
Students are able to account for losses in the calculation of simple frictional pipe flows.
Students are able to analyze compressible, isentropic flows along a streamline with respect to subsonic/supersonic conditions, shock waves, and expansions.
Students are able to calculate one-dimensional flows in nozzles and diffusers for given contours.
Students are able to name relevant measurement techniques and instruments of experimental fluid mechanics.
Students are able to derive similarity laws from dimensionless numbers.
Students are able to independently solve application-oriented tasks (in homework) with the knowledge acquired in the lecture and the methods and procedures practiced in the tutorials.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and importance of Fluid Mechanics in nature and technology
Flow Kinematics, Introduction to Hydrodynamics / Aerodynamics
